blocks.text: 世界卫生组织（WHO）估计，全球每年有超过25万例可预防的死亡由妊娠相关并发症导致。虽然产前超声可以改善妊娠结局并降低胎儿和孕产妇死亡率，但全球三分之二的人口无法获得超声等诊断性医学影像。当前支持孕产妇健康的方法严重依赖专业临床培训，导致数百万生活在资源匮乏地区的人在 entire pregnancy 期间都无法获得一次超声检查。

blocks.text: 我们看到了一个机会，可以开展研究来满足这一现实需求，即开发能够解读“盲扫”超声的机器学习系统。这种扫描方式让未接受过专业超声培训的一线医护人员只需以标准化模式将低成本、便携式超声探头在腹部滑动即可完成扫描。

blocks.text: 为评估高效的系统调优，该研究利用来自芝加哥的 120 名参与者的小型试点数据集——约为原始训练集的 6%——使模型适应新的探头硬件，并将孕龄预测范围扩展到 36 周以上。为理解泛化能力，内罗毕站点的数据未用于微调，从而保持肯尼亚临床验证为严格独立的外部测试。为评估综合效用，该研究还纳入了多胎妊娠，这可能给人工操作者和自动化系统带来追踪和测量挑战。

blocks.text: 该诊断研究评估了 385 名孕 16 至 36 周参与者的主要队列，展示了强有力的 AI 系统结果：

inlines.text: 该诊断研究评估了 385 名孕 16 至 36 周参与者的主要队列，展示了强有力的 AI 系统结果：
临床非劣效准确性
：在两个队列中，AI 模型估计孕龄的平均绝对误差（MAE）为 4.18 天，成功证明其不劣于由专家超声技师执行的标准临床程序，后者的 MAE 为 4.48 天。
跨场景泛化
：在芝加哥，适配后的模型 MAE 为 4.10 天。在内罗毕，在零本地优化的情况下，模型达到了相当的 MAE 4.27 天。

blocks.text: 除了凸显通过 AI 扩大超声可及性的巨大机会外，这项前瞻性多中心研究还使我们能够主动观察并优化 AI 在真实临床环境中的行为。通过将我们的系统直接部署到日常临床工作流程中，我们获得了有助于面向真实世界使用进行设计的实用见解。例如，我们观察到在连续患者之间保持设备充电时，可更换电池比插入式充电底座更重要。

blocks.text: 这些研究还表明，部署此类 AI 系统还需要与临床医生和患者建立深度信任。最终实现这一目标的一个重要方式是在应用中内置明确的保障措施，例如由我们的模型生成模型置信度估计，以拒绝质量差的扫描并向临床医生用户传达模型不确定性。

blocks.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that more than 250,000 preventable deaths occur worldwide each year due to pregnancy-related complications. While prenatal ultrasound can improve outcomes and reduce fetal and maternal mortality, two-thirds of people globally lack access to diagnostic medical imaging like ultrasound. Current methods that support maternal health rely heavily on specialized clinical training, leaving millions in low-resource settings without access to a single ultrasound during their entire pregnancy.

This way of scanning allows frontline healthcare workers without specialized sonography training to perform scans by simply gliding low-cost, portable ultrasound probes across the abdomen in a standardized pattern.

blocks.text: In “Generalization of AI-Based Gestational Age Assessment Using Blind Sweep Ultrasonography”, published in JAMA Network Open, we evaluated how effectively an AI model for gestational age assessment (how far along the pregnancy is) generalizes across diverse clinical settings and hardware. While our previous research validated the model's performance on unseen patients from the same retrospective cohort it learned from, this new prospective study shows how the AI system performs reliably running live on mobile devices in real clinics, with only novice operators and unfamiliar ultrasound equipment, and minimal fine-tuning.

blocks.text: For a medical AI system to safely scale globally, it must demonstrate generalizability — maintaining accurate diagnostic performance when introduced to new clinical settings with different patient populations, clinical workflows, and ultrasound hardware variations than those on which the model was trained.

blocks.text: Originally trained on ultrasound data collected in North Carolina and Zambia using a set of Sonosite, GE, and Butterfly Networks commercial ultrasound probes, the research AI system was paired with Clarius C3, a commercial handheld transabdominal probe. All of these sites differed in various care dimensions, including when women first come in for prenatal care, how many routine ultrasounds they receive, and how gestational age is usually dated.

blocks.text: To evaluate efficient system tuning, the study leveraged a small pilot dataset of 120 participants from Chicago — approximately 6% of the original training set—to adapt the model to new probe hardware and extend the gestational age prediction range beyond 36 weeks. To understand generalizability, no data from the Nairobi site was used for fine-tuning, maintaining the Kenyan clinical validation as a strictly independent, external test. To evaluate comprehensive utility, the study also included multiple gestation pregnancies, which could present tracking and measurement challenges for both human operators and automated systems.

blocks.text: Key findings: Matching the expert standard

inlines.text: Key findings: Matching the expert standard

blocks.text: We compared the AI system’s ability to estimate fetal age from blind sweep ultrasounds to formula-based estimation from the clinically standard expert approach. This expert approach relies on an expert sonographer locating multiple specific cross-sections of the fetus(es) to take precise biometry measurements, a difficult-to-scale task that requires years of training and is highly operator-dependent.

blocks.text: Evaluating a primary cohort of 385 participants between 16 and 36 weeks of pregnancy, the diagnostic study demonstrated strong AI system results:

inlines.text: Evaluating a primary cohort of 385 participants between 16 and 36 weeks of pregnancy, the diagnostic study demonstrated strong AI system results:
Clinically non-inferior accuracy

: Across both cohorts, the AI model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.18 days in estimating gestational age, successfully demonstrating non-inferiority to the standard clinical procedure performed by expert sonographers, which had an MAE of 4.48 days.
Cross-setting generalization
: In Chicago, the adapted model achieved an MAE of 4.10 days. In Nairobi, with zero local optimization, the model achieved a comparable MAE of 4.27 days.

blocks.text: Beyond accuracy, exploratory metrics showed that the research AI system was resilient in complex scenarios. For instance, in cases of fetal weight extremes (above the 90th percentile), the model outperformed traditional biometry formulas, demonstrating robustness against variations in fetal size.

blocks.text: Lessons learned during prospective deployment

inlines.text: Lessons learned during prospective deployment

blocks.text: In addition to highlighting an immense opportunity to expand ultrasound access through AI, the prospective multi-center study allowed us to actively observe and optimize how AI behaves in live clinical environments. By deploying our system directly into everyday clinical workflows, we gained practical insights that help us design for real world use. For example, we observed the importance of swappable batteries over plug-in docking stations for keeping devices charged between consecutive patients.

blocks.text: These studies also demonstrated how deploying AI systems like this will also require building deep trust with both clinicians and patients. One important way to ultimately achieve this would be by building clear safeguards into the app, like model confidence estimates produced by our model to reject poor-quality sweeps and convey model uncertainty to the clinician user.

blocks.text: Looking ahead: Expanding access to care with AI

inlines.text: Looking ahead: Expanding access to care with AI

blocks.text: These study findings indicate that AI-based systems can analyze standardized “blind sweeps” images acquired by operators without specialized sonography training. The AI estimate of fetal age had accuracy comparable to the current standard of care from expert operators and more expensive traditional, cart-based ultrasound machines. Demonstrating technical generalizability across diverse clinical settings, hardware, and changing populations, marks a key step in highlighting their potential to expand access to this critical capability for maternal health.

blocks.text: By empowering minimally trained community health workers to perform reliable ultrasonography assessments, this research demonstrates the potential to expand prenatal coverage for millions in under-resourced areas. Studying the capabilities of this scalable technology lays the groundwork for more resilient, accessible healthcare systems, ensuring that every mother, regardless of location, has the chance for a healthy pregnancy and a safe delivery.

The insights gained from this research inform the development of our next-generation, multimodal medical intelligence research. Through our continued work, we strive to provide the development community and scientists with the answers they need to improve clinical care and make it helpful and accessible to all.
